purpose: Store mathematical representations separately from curriculum expectations and teacher moves so MathBridge can explain what a representation makes visible, when it helps, and how its use is evidenced across systems.

evidence_policy.rule: Do not treat the presence of a representation in one official document as proof that all teachers in that jurisdiction use it frequently.
evidence_policy.country_comparison_rule: Representations are compared by documented curriculum/guidance use and pedagogical function, not by stereotypes about national teaching style.
evidence_policy.us_rule: Common Core specifies some representations but explicitly does not prescribe a full teaching method; IES/WWC guidance supplies separate evidence about instructional use.
evidence_policy.cn_rule: Current PEP evidence supports structured, connected, multi-representational and exploratory design, but representation-by-grade claims require direct current-volume or teacher-guide evidence.

representations.name_cn: 数的组成 / 部分—部分—整体模型
teacher_moves: ask pupils to identify the whole and parts
write multiple equations for the same structure
hide one part and reason from known relationships
common_misconceptions: treating the diagram as decoration rather than a mathematical relationship
assuming subtraction is only take-away rather than finding a missing part or difference

CN.evidence: Current PEP Grade 1 design integrates number meaning, composition, addition and subtraction in connected units; exact diagram naming/frequency remains volume-level evidence.

UK.evidence: DfE guidance explicitly develops addition and subtraction through part–part–whole structure and connects equations to diagrams.

US.evidence: Common Core includes putting-together, taking-apart and compare problem structures with unknowns in varied positions, supported by objects, drawings and equations.

teacher_moves: ask what pupils can see without counting one-by-one
compare two arrangements for the same number
scale the value represented by each counter while preserving the frame structure
common_misconceptions: using the frame only for counting rather than seeing structure
changing layouts so frequently that pupils cannot internalise five-and-ten structure

CN.evidence: Do not infer current PEP ten-frame use without direct page/teacher-guide evidence.

UK.evidence: DfE primary guidance explicitly uses tens frames and counters from Year 1 and reuses the same structure with scaled place values in later years.

US.evidence: Common Core supports concrete models and drawings for base-ten reasoning but does not require the ten-frame as a named representation.

representations.name_cn: 十进位值模型 / 位值学具
teacher_moves: compose ten smaller units into one larger unit
decompose one larger unit when regrouping
connect each physical/pictorial action to a written equation or algorithm
common_misconceptions: pupils manipulating blocks procedurally without linking them to place value
failing to distinguish unit size from number of units

CN.evidence: Current PEP foregrounds counting units as a structural thread across whole numbers, decimals, fractions and operations; exact manipulatives require textbook/teacher-guide evidence.

UK.evidence: DfE guidance uses place-value counters, bundled units and scaled tens-frame structures to expose powers-of-ten relationships.

US.evidence: Common Core repeatedly requires base-ten understanding and allows concrete models/drawings; IES recommends well-chosen concrete and semi-concrete representations.

teacher_moves: use marked and unmarked number lines
reason from endpoints and midpoints instead of counting ticks
connect position to magnitude and distance
vary endpoints and intervals
common_misconceptions: treating ticks as objects to count rather than locations
assuming a fraction number line always runs from 0 to 1
unequal spacing

CN.evidence: PEP has a long-standing documented use of objects, pictures, figures and number lines for number concepts; current 12th-series grade-specific use needs direct evidence.

UK.evidence: DfE introduces number lines explicitly for order and relative size in Year 1 and extends them to fractions, decimals, rounding and proportional reasoning.

US.evidence: Common Core explicitly requires number-line diagrams for whole-number operations, fractions and later rational numbers; IES gives number-line use strong evidence in elementary intervention.

teacher_moves: describe rows and columns
rotate arrays to discuss commutativity
partition arrays to expose distributivity
connect equal groups to area
common_misconceptions: counting individual objects instead of using group structure
confusing number of groups with group size

CN.evidence: Use must be verified from current PEP multiplication units before claiming a grade-specific sequence.

UK.evidence: Arrays form part of the representation repertoire used in primary multiplication guidance/resources; exact use should be attached to specific DfE/NCETM locators when surfaced.

US.evidence: Common Core uses rectangular arrays in Grade 2 as equal-addend structure and as a foundation for multiplication and area.

representations.name_cn: 条形模型 / 线段图式模型
teacher_moves: translate a context into quantities and relationships before calculating
label known and unknown quantities
ask what each bar or segment represents
compare the model with an equation
common_misconceptions: teaching the bar model as a fixed recipe
drawing bars not proportional to the intended relationship when proportionality matters
moving to calculation before interpreting the model

CN.evidence: Chinese primary mathematics has a broader diagrammatic/problem-structure tradition, but current PEP bar/segment-model claims require direct textbook evidence rather than analogy.

UK.evidence: NCETM explicitly describes the bar model as a representation for exposing mathematical structure rather than a solution method; DfE guidance uses bar models for division, fractions and unknowns.

US.evidence: Common Core defines a visual fraction model as including a tape diagram, number-line diagram or area model; tape diagrams also fit its modelling and representation practices.

teacher_moves: partition a rectangle by place value or fractional parts
connect each region to a partial product
recombine regions into an equation
compare area and symbolic methods
common_misconceptions: treating partition lines as arbitrary
losing the connection between dimensions and factors
using the model after pupils no longer understand what each region represents

CN.evidence: Current PEP emphasises structural connections and modelling, but representation-specific grade use requires direct current-volume verification.

UK.evidence: DfE/NCETM primary materials use rectangular/partitioned structures in multiplication and fractions; exact locator should accompany publication-level claims.

US.evidence: Common Core explicitly includes area models within visual fraction models and uses area/array structure to connect multiplication and fractions.

representations.name_cn: 部分积 / 展开式计算方法
teacher_moves: name the value of each partial product
connect partial products to an array or area partition
compare expanded and compact written forms
ask why regrouping or recombination is valid
common_misconceptions: treating partial products as an extra algorithm to memorise
failing to connect each line to place value
keeping transitional recording after it stops adding conceptual value

CN.evidence: Current PEP multiplication-unit restructuring is verified, but exact expanded-method sequence requires direct teacher-guide evidence.

UK.evidence: DfE guidance develops calculation methods through place-value structure toward efficient formal written methods.

US.evidence: Common Core explicitly maintains place-value/properties-based strategies before mandatory standard algorithms in later grades.

teacher_moves: connect each written step to place value and prior representations
compare efficiency with mental or expanded methods
use estimation to check reasonableness
ask pupils to explain regrouping and intermediate values
common_misconceptions: introducing the compact algorithm before pupils understand place value
teaching carrying/borrowing as unexplained digit manipulation
assuming procedural fluency proves conceptual understanding

CN.evidence: Algorithm fluency is an important part of Chinese primary mathematics, but current PEP 12th-series introduction points must be verified volume by volume.

UK.evidence: DfE statutory/guidance progression explicitly moves into formal columnar and formal multiplication/division methods across primary years.

US.evidence: Common Core specifies conceptual and strategy development first and mandates particular standard algorithms at later grade points for major whole-number operations.
